anguilla.title: Flag of Anguilla

colors.note: The Union Jack in the canton.
The three dolphins in the coat of arms.

desc:
- A Blue Ensign defaced with the coat of arms of Anguilla, featuring three orange dolphins
- The dolphins symbolise endurance, unity, and strength
- **Construction:** a standard Blue Ensign (1:2 ratio) with the Union Flag in the canton occupying one-quarter of the field
- The badge of Anguilla (three dolphins) is centred in the fly half
trivia:
- The dolphins represent grace and swiftness; the orange, blue, green, and white show Caribbean colours
- Adopted in 1990 after Anguilla separated from St. Kitts and Nevis
- The dolphins are stylized versions of spotted dolphins found in Caribbean waters around Anguilla

anguilla-dolphin.title: Dolphin Flag of Anguilla

colors.note: Turquoise-to-navy sea at the bottom; represents the surrounding Caribbean Sea.
Three dolphins; represent friendship, wisdom, and strength.

desc:
- An unofficial local flag of Anguilla featuring three orange dolphins arranged in a circle on a white field above a turquoise sea
- The three dolphins symbolise friendship, wisdom, and strength — the three core values of the Anguillan people
- This flag is used locally alongside the official British Blue Ensign variant
- **Construction:** a white field with the lower portion rendered as a turquoise sea. Three orange dolphins are centred, leaping in a circle. Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- Alternative Anguilla flag design emphasizing the dolphin symbolism
- Dolphins are central to Anguillian maritime culture and identity
- This flag variant celebrates the island's marine biodiversity

anguilla-governor.title: Flag of the Governor of Anguilla
desc:
- The Governor's flag of Anguilla is a Union Flag (Union Jack) defaced with the Anguillan coat of arms on a white disc in the centre
- It represents the Governor as the representative of the British Crown in Anguilla, a British Overseas Territory
- The coat of arms features three orange dolphins in a circle
- **Construction:** the Union Flag at full size, with a white disc bearing the coat of arms superimposed at the centre. Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- Official flag used by the Governor of Anguilla
- Represents executive authority and British colonial ties
- Uses heraldic symbols reflecting Anguilla's governance structure
